intro.author: Traditionally Moses, whose speeches fill most of the book; the account of his death (ch. 34) was written by someone else. Many scholars think the book reached its final form centuries later.
intro.written: Traditionally at the end of Moses' life, on the plains of Moab; many scholars date its final form to the 600s BC, around King Josiah's reforms
intro.audience: The new generation of Israel, about to cross the Jordan after their parents' generation died in the wilderness
intro.setting: Forty years after leaving Egypt, Israel is camped on the plains of Moab, east of the Jordan and across from Jericho. Moses, now 120 and not permitted to enter the land, gives a series of farewell speeches that renew the covenant first made at Mount Horeb (Sinai).
intro.purpose: To renew the covenant with a generation that had not stood at Horeb, and to prepare them to stay loyal to the Lord once they were settled and prosperous in Canaan.
intro.bigIdea: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, and remember what he has done, so that you may live in the land he gives.
